checked.found: Legend (Lucian, Plutarch variants) has the runner carry news of the victory at Marathon (490 BCE) to Athens, about 40 km, and die; description is hedged with 'Legend says'. Herodotus only records the Athens-Sparta run.

Sources agree Augustus founded it but date it loosely to his reign (27 BCE-14 CE); Suetonius-based accounts give about 20 BCE. -27 is the start of his reign, not a sourced founding year. Wagons/riders/stations claims are supported.
Sources credit Ogedei (reign from 1229) with founding or formalising the yam, but give no exact year; a rudimentary system existed under Genghis Khan.

Armada sighted off the Lizard 19 July 1588 and beacons lit, so year and name are fine. But no source supports 'across England within hours'; one account has Elizabeth at Richmond alerted about three days later.
Charles I opened the royal post to the public on 31 July 1635; fees set by distance (and number of sheets).
Trial run 2 August 1784 with armed guards replacing post-boys. Route was Bristol (via Bath) to London; description's 'two English cities' holds. The slug says Bath-London, which is not player-facing.
Paris-Lille line with arm-and-crossbar towers; first official message August 1794; a message took about half an hour.
Patent 10 June 1837; needle telegraph pointing to letters; first demonstrated on the London and Birmingham Railway, adopted by GWR.
First ride 3 April 1860 from St. Joseph, Missouri to Sacramento, California, with relay stations every 10-15 miles.
First experimental RFD routes began 1 October 1896 in West Virginia (Charles Town, Halltown, Uvilla).
12 December 1901, Marconi received the faint Morse letter S from Poldhu at Signal Hill, Newfoundland.
18 February 1911, Henri Pequet, Allahabad, part of the U.P. Exhibition, about 6,000 letters and postcards.

Year 1918 (Lost Battalion, 4 October) is right, and the wounded-bird claims match. But a Smithsonian DNA analysis found Cher Ami was male, so 'Her' is wrong. (Whether Cher Ami carried the key message is also disputed by the National Archives.)
Public London-New York radiotelephone service opened 7 January 1927 at about $25 a minute / $75 for three minutes.
China Clipper (Martin M-130 flying boat) left Alameda, California on 22 November 1935 carrying airmail to Manila.
Opened 25 September 1956 with 36 channels, first transatlantic telephone cable, replacing radio-based service.
Five-digit ZIP Code launched 1 July 1963, designed for automated sorting.
Founded 1969 in San Francisco by Dalsey, Hillblom and Lynn, flying bills of lading to Honolulu.
17 April 1973: 14 aircraft flew 186 packages from Memphis to 25 US cities.
Western Union ended telegram service with a notice effective 27 January 2006.
First Prime Air customer delivery 7 December 2016, to a rural customer near Cambridge, England.
